text: {"answer": "The evidence is mixed and depends on context. A meta-analysis summary reports a net positive effect of remote work on individual output, with a median of +10% for focused tasks and -4% for collaborative tasks [d658dc380b73#5]. The same source notes that the net effect depends on the mix of focused and collaborative work in a role [d658dc380b73#5]. A randomized trial at Trip.com found that a hybrid schedule showed no measurable productivity difference from fully in-office peers [d658dc380b73#5]. A field experiment on discretionary remote work found that about two remote days per week was preferred and helped mothers without harming non-mothers [ef88116f982d#0]. However, a study of full-time remote work (five days a week) reported an association with reduced work productivity and higher presenteeism [abefd158b9c2#2].
